headline: Cell-type-resolved models score noncoding variant effects on regulatory activity
label: Regulatory Variant Effect Modeling
summary: Single-cell atlases and sequence-based variant models now resolve noncoding regulatory effects across brain, blood, and cancer cell states.
synthesis: Across these studies, the dominant thread is sequence-to-activity modeling used to attribute noncoding variation to regulatory state in defined cellular contexts. AlphaGenome 2 predicts cell-type-conditioned regulatory activity and variant effects from 1-Mb DNA and adds an enhancer-gene link atlas. ChromBPNet scores 302,830 noncoding variants across 17 hematopoietic cell types, reporting lineage-structured accessibility effects that are complementary to GWAS. Single-cell multi-omic atlases of the adult human brain, human basal ganglia, and adult mouse brain map histone marks, accessibility and 3D genome, with a sequence-to-function variant model in the first. A pan-cancer single-cell lncRNA atlas links lncRNAs to regulons and CRISPR screens. What is new is cell-state conditioning of sequence-based variant prediction, paired with experimental readouts that couple genetic edits to single-cell expression: Superb-seq captures Cas9 edits and transcriptomes jointly, and Perturb-Tags reveals non-autonomous responses in spatial screens.
